topic.seo_description: Explore KRAS mutations in pancreatic, colorectal, and lung cancers. Discover latest biomarker research, diagnostic advances, and targeted treatment developments.
topic.seo_intro:
KRAS is one of the most frequently mutated oncogenes in human cancer, playing a critical role in the development and progression of several aggressive cancer types, particularly pancreatic, colorectal, and lung cancers. This gene normally acts as a molecular switch controlling cell growth and division, but when mutated, it becomes permanently activated, driving uncontrolled cell proliferation. Understanding KRAS mutations has become increasingly important for cancer researchers and clinicians because these mutations can serve as valuable biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection.

The study of KRAS mutations represents a significant area of cancer research innovation. For decades, KRAS was considered "undruggable," but recent breakthrough discoveries have led to the development of targeted therapies specifically designed to inhibit mutated KRAS proteins. These advances are opening new possibilities for patients whose tumors harbor KRAS mutations. Additionally, KRAS testing has become a standard diagnostic tool, helping oncologists identify patients who may benefit from precision medicine approaches and enabling more personalized treatment strategies.

On this page, you'll find comprehensive information about KRAS mutations, their role as cancer biomarkers, the latest diagnostic techniques for detecting KRAS alterations, and current research exploring novel therapeutic approaches. Whether you're a patient, caregiver, or healthcare provider seeking to understand this important oncogene, our curated collection of articles below represents the latest peer-reviewed research findings and clinical developments in KRAS-related cancer research.

articles.title: A targeted combination therapy achieves effective pancreatic cancer regression and prevents tumor resistance.
articles.hook: KRAS-EGFR-STAT3 triple therapy eliminates pancreatic tumors and prevents drug resistance
articles.summary: Combining three targeted drugs—targeting KRAS, EGFR, and STAT3—completely shrinks pancreatic tumors and prevents treatment resistance.

articles.title: Standard Versus Reduced Sotorasib Dosing in KRAS G12C-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis-Have We Answered the Dosing Question?
articles.hook: Lower sotorasib doses match standard doses in KRAS G12C lung cancer
articles.summary: Sotorasib's standard lung cancer dose may be unnecessarily high; lower doses show similar benefits with fewer side effects.

articles.title: KRAS G12R in Pancreatic Cancer: Why this Mutation Resists Current Inhibitor Strategies.
articles.hook: KRAS G12R mutation resists current inhibitor drugs in pancreatic cancer
articles.summary: A common pancreatic cancer KRAS mutation (G12R) resists current inhibitor drugs that work in other cancer types.

articles.title: Mevalonate pathway rewiring driven by enhancer remodelling confers resistance to KRAS inhibitors in colorectal cancer.
articles.hook: Statins restore KRAS inhibitor effectiveness in resistant colorectal cancer cells
articles.summary: Colorectal cancer cells resist KRAS inhibitors by rewiring cholesterol production; combining statins with KRAS inhibitors restores treatment effectiveness.

articles.title: Monoclonal antibodies targeting PCDH7 inhibit tumor growth and enhance immune responses in KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
articles.hook: PCDH7-targeting antibodies shrink KRAS-mutant lung tumors
articles.summary: Antibodies targeting PCDH7 shrink KRAS-mutant lung tumors and boost immune responses in preclinical models.

articles.title: KRAS4A promotes oligomerization of hexokinase 1 on mitochondria.
articles.hook: Researchers discovered that KRAS4A protein increases clustering of hexokinase 1 on mitochondria, enhancing cancer cell energy production.
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that KRAS4A protein increases clustering of hexokinase 1 on mitochondria, enhancing cancer cell energy production.

articles.title: Convergence of KRAS Mutations and MTAP Loss in Pancreatic Cancer: Genomic Landscape and Clinical Implications.
articles.hook: KRAS mutations combined with MTAP loss define pancreatic cancer subtypes
articles.summary: Pancreatic cancer patients with specific genetic mutations show improved outcomes through comprehensive genomic profiling for personalized treatment planning.
